CANDIDATE_FORMULATION_UNDER_ATTACK: a functional organising system generates a spatially distinct second organising system of the same operational class, using newly maintained material, and the second system can persist functionally without depending on the continued functioning of the original

ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.attack: 'of the same operational class' is undefined
ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.response: it is defined operationally here as satisfying the same frozen functional maturation criterion the first centre satisfies: a qualified local X response held for T_primary steps. No new predicate is introduced.

ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.attack: 'newly maintained material' invites an arbitrary percentage
ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.response: it is replaced by a threshold-free comparison against the certified upper bound on surviving pre-separation material, derived from muX alone.

ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.attack: 'without depending on the continued functioning of the original' is causal and cannot be read off passive data
ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.response: correct, and this is the decisive limitation. It is why R2 is separated out and why RCD01 does not claim it.

ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.attack: the formulation says nothing about generations
ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.response: deliberate. Generation competence is R3 and is argued to be beyond the MINIMUM first-generation criterion.

ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.attack: the formulation could be satisfied by a fission of one cloud into two halves
ATTACKS_ON_THE_CANDIDATE.response: that is exactly what R1 excludes: a halved cloud is old material, and the certified bound rejects it.

LEVELS.name: FUNCTIONAL_MULTIPLICATION
LEVELS.scientific_meaning: one functional organising centre becomes two functional organising centres
LEVELS.necessary: yes — nothing called reproduction can require less
LEVELS.sufficient: no — a system can multiply centres without any of them being new in substance or independent
LEVELS.evidence: 53 of 192 fresh worlds; the FDFLT01 qualified claim

LEVELS.name: MATERIAL_RECONSTRUCTION
LEVELS.scientific_meaning: the new centre's functional X field cannot be accounted for by redistributed pre-separation material
LEVELS.necessary: yes — otherwise a cloud that merely splits would count
LEVELS.sufficient: no — new material does not imply causal independence
LEVELS.observable_in_current_data: yes, as a certified lower bound
LEVELS.evidence: 25 of 53 R0 worlds satisfy the threshold-free bound; the count is a lower bound because the bound credits the daughter with every surviving old molecule in the world

LEVELS.name: FUNCTIONAL_INDEPENDENCE
LEVELS.scientific_meaning: after the new centre matures, removing or inactivating the original centre does not destroy the new centre's qualified X response over a physically derived hold interval
LEVELS.necessary: yes — this is the causal content of the word reproduction
LEVELS.sufficient: together with R0 and R1, yes, for a MINIMAL first-generation claim
LEVELS.evidence: no world in any dataset had one centre removed while another persisted; the only executable intervention zeroes the entire Y field

LEVELS.name: REPRODUCTIVE_COMPETENCE
LEVELS.scientific_meaning: a centre that arose as the second functional centre itself participates in generating a further functional centre
LEVELS.necessary: no for a minimal first-generation claim; yes for a strong self-reproduction claim
LEVELS.requires_intervention: no, but it requires lifting the stop rule
LEVELS.evidence: 25 worlds reach a third centre and 20 of them had two functional centres first, but the frozen stop rule ends every world at the third centre, so 0 of 25 have enough record left for the third centre to mature

SELECTED_HIERARCHY.STRONG_SELF_REPRODUCTION: R0 and R1 and R2 and R3
SELECTED_HIERARCHY.HEREDITY: a separate future criterion, not part of either

ALTERNATIVES_CONSIDERED_AND_REJECTED.rejected_because: a second centre that dies the moment the first is removed was never an independent system; without R2 the word reproduction carries no causal content
a cloud that splits in two and both halves persist would qualify, which is division of substance, not production of new substance
requiring the daughter to reproduce before the first event counts as reproduction is an infinite regress; R3 is the right criterion for a STRONG claim, not the minimum

ALTERNATIVES_CONSIDERED_AND_REJECTED.alternative: require survival of the original founder particle
ALTERNATIVES_CONSIDERED_AND_REJECTED.rejected_because: already rejected by FLCR01; particle identity is not organisational identity
